questions.q: The angle between the lines whose direction ratios are $a,b,c$ and $b-c,c-a,a-b$ is
questions.explanation: Dot product $=a(b-c)+b(c-a)+c(a-b)=0$, so the lines are perpendicular, i.e. angle $=90^\circ$.

questions.q: The measure of the angle between the lines $x=k-1,y=2k+1,z=2k+3, k\in\mathbb R$ and $\dfrac{x+1}{2}=\dfrac{y-2}{1}=\dfrac{z-1}{2}$ is
questions.explanation: Direction ratios are $(1,2,2)$ and $(2,1,2)$. $\cos\theta=\dfrac{1(2)+2(1)+2(2)}{3\times3}=\dfrac89$.

questions.q: If a line makes angles $90^\circ, 60^\circ$ and $\theta$ with x, y and z axes respectively, where $\theta$ is acute, then the value of $\theta$ is
questions.explanation: $\cos^290+\cos^260+\cos^2\theta=1 \Rightarrow \cos^2\theta=3/4\Rightarrow\theta=\pi/6$.

questions.q: The equation of the line through the point (0, 1, 2) and perpendicular to the line $\dfrac{x-1}{2}=\dfrac{y+1}{3}=\dfrac{z-1}{-2}$ is
questions.explanation: Direction ratios must satisfy 2d1+3d2-2d3=0; only (-3,4,3) among the options satisfies this.

questions.q: If lines $\dfrac{x-1}{-3}=\dfrac{y-2}{2k}=\dfrac{z-3}{2}$ and $\dfrac{x-1}{3k}=\dfrac{y-5}{1}=\dfrac{z-6}{-5}$ are mutually perpendicular, then $k$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Perpendicularity gives $(-3)(3k)+(2k)(1)+(2)(-5)=0 \Rightarrow -9k+2k-10=0 \Rightarrow k=-\dfrac{10}{7}$.

questions.q: If a line makes an angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ with each X and Y axis then the acute angle made by Z-axis is
questions.explanation: $\cos^2\alpha+\cos^2\beta+\cos^2\gamma=1$ with $\alpha=\beta=\pi/3$ gives $\cos^2\gamma=1/2$, so $\gamma=\pi/4$.

questions.q: The length of perpendicular drawn from the point $(3, -1, 11)$ to the line $\dfrac{x}{2} = \dfrac{y-2}{3} = \dfrac{z-3}{4}$ is
questions.explanation: Using $d = \dfrac{|\vec{AP}\times\vec d|}{|\vec d|}$ with $\vec{AP}=(3,-3,8)$ and $\vec d=(2,3,4)$ gives $d=\sqrt{1537/29}=\sqrt{53}$.

questions.q: The equation of the plane through the points $(2, 1, 0), (3, 2, -2)$ and $(3, 1, 7)$ is
The point of intersection of the line $x + 1 = \dfrac{y+3}{3} = \dfrac{-z+2}{2}$ with the plane $3x + 4y + 5z = 10$ is
questions.explanation: Parametrize $x=-1+t, y=-3+3t, z=2-2t$; substituting into the plane gives $t=3$, so the point is $(2,6,-4)$.

questions.q: If $(2, 3, -1)$ is the foot of the perpendicular from $(4, 2, 1)$ to a plane, then the equation of the plane is
The distance of the point whose position vector is $(2\hat i + \hat j - \hat k)$ from the plane $\vec r\cdot(\hat i - 2\hat j + 4\hat k) = 4$ is
The co-ordinates of foot of the perpendicular drawn from the origin to the plane 2x - 3y + 4z = 29 are
questions.explanation: Foot $=\left(\frac{2d}{29},\frac{-3d}{29},\frac{4d}{29}\right)$ with $d=29$, giving (2, -3, 4).

questions.q: The angle between the pair of lines $\dfrac{x+3}{3}=\dfrac{y-1}{5}=\dfrac{z+3}{4}$ and $\dfrac{x+1}{1}=\dfrac{y-4}{4}=\dfrac{z-5}{2}$ is
questions.explanation: Using direction ratios (3,5,4) and (1,4,2), $\cos\theta=\dfrac{31}{5\sqrt{42}}\approx0.957$, which does not match any of the printed options exactly — this appears to be a defective question (matching numbers do not exist among the choices), consistent with the KEA grace mark. Option (C) is closest numerically. (as per KEA key)

questions.q: The equation of the line joining the points ($-$3, 4, 11) and (1, $-$2, 7) is
questions.explanation: Direction ratios are (4,$-$6,$-$4), i.e. (2,$-$3,$-$2) or equivalently ($-$2,3,2), giving the equation in option B.

questions.q: The angle between the lines whose direction cosines are $\left(\dfrac{\sqrt3}{4},\dfrac14,\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)$ and $\left(\dfrac{\sqrt3}{4},\dfrac14,\dfrac{-\sqrt3}{2}\right)$ is
questions.explanation: cos$\theta$ = 3/16+1/16$-$3/4 = $-1/2$; taking the acute angle between the lines (absolute value), $\theta=\pi/3$.

questions.q: If a plane meets the coordinate axes at A, B and C in such a way that the centroid of triangle ABC is at the point (1, 2, 3) then the equation of the plane is
questions.explanation: With intercepts p,q,r, centroid = (p/3,q/3,r/3) = (1,2,3) gives p=3,q=6,r=9, so the plane is x/3+y/6+z/9=1.

questions.q: If a line makes an angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ with each of $x$ and $y$-axis, then the acute angle made by z-axis is
questions.explanation: $\cos^2(\pi/3)+\cos^2(\pi/3)+\cos^2\gamma=1\Rightarrow \cos^2\gamma=1/2\Rightarrow\gamma=\pi/4$ (question was given a grace mark by KEA).

questions.q: The distance of the point $(1, 2, -4)$ from the line $\dfrac{x-3}{2}=\dfrac{y-3}{3}=\dfrac{z+5}{6}$ is
questions.explanation: With point-on-line $(3,3,-5)$ and direction $(2,3,6)$, the perpendicular distance formula gives $\sqrt{293}/7$.

questions.q: The sine of the angle between the straight line $\dfrac{x-2}{3}=\dfrac{3-y}{-4}=\dfrac{z-4}{5}$ and the plane $2x-2y+z=5$ is
questions.explanation: Direction $(3,4,5)$, normal $(2,-2,1)$; $\sin\theta=\dfrac{|6-8+5|}{\sqrt{50}\cdot3}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{50}}=\dfrac{\sqrt2}{10}$.

questions.q: Foot of the perpendicular drawn from the point $(1,3,4)$ to the plane $2x-y+z+3=0$ is
Acute angle between the line $\dfrac{x-5}{2}=\dfrac{y+1}{-1}=\dfrac{z+4}{1}$ and the plane $3x-4y-z+5=0$ is
questions.explanation: $\sin\theta=\dfrac{|\vec a\cdot \vec n|}{|\vec a||\vec n|}=\dfrac{9}{\sqrt{156}}$; writing $\cos\theta=\sqrt{1-\sin^2\theta}$ simplifies to $\dfrac{5}{2\sqrt{13}}$, giving $\theta=\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{5}{2\sqrt{13}}\right)$.

questions.q: The distance of the point $(1,2,1)$ from the line $\dfrac{x-1}{2}=\dfrac{y-2}{1}=\dfrac{z-3}{2}$ is
questions.explanation: With a point on the line $(1,2,3)$ and direction $(2,1,2)$, the perpendicular distance is $\dfrac{|(0,0,-2)\times(2,1,2)|}{|(2,1,2)|}=\dfrac{2\sqrt5}{3}$.

questions.q: XY-plane divides the line joining the points $A(2,3,-5)$ and $B(-1,-2,-3)$ in the ratio
questions.explanation: The ratio is $-z_1:z_2 = 5:-3$; the negative sign shows the division is external, i.e. $5:3$ externally.

questions.q: The image of the point $(1,6,3)$ in the line $\dfrac{x}{1}=\dfrac{y-1}{2}=\dfrac{z-2}{3}$ is
questions.explanation: The foot of perpendicular is $(1,3,5)$ (at $t=1$); the image is $2(1,3,5)-(1,6,3)=(1,0,7)$.

questions.q: The angle between the lines $2x=3y=-z$ and $6x=-y=-4z$ is
questions.explanation: Direction ratios are $(3,2,-6)$ and $(2,-12,-3)$; their dot product is 0, so the lines are perpendicular.

questions.q: The value of k such that the line $\dfrac{x-4}{1}=\dfrac{y-2}{1}=\dfrac{z-k}{2}$ lies on the plane $2x-4y+z=7$ is
questions.explanation: The point $(4,2,k)$ must satisfy the plane: $8-8+k=7\Rightarrow k=7$ (and the direction vector is perpendicular to the normal).

questions.q: The locus represented by $xy+yz=0$ is
questions.explanation: $y(x+z)=0$ gives planes $y=0$ and $x+z=0$, whose normals $(0,1,0)$ and $(1,0,1)$ are perpendicular (dot product 0).

questions.q: Reflexion of the point $(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$ in XY plane is
questions.explanation: Reflection in the XY-plane keeps x and y unchanged and reverses the sign of z.

questions.q: The plane $2x-3y+6z-11=0$ makes an angle $\sin^{-1}(\alpha)$ with X-axis. The value of $\alpha$ is equal to
questions.explanation: The normal vector $(2,-3,6)$ has magnitude 7; the angle the plane makes with the x-axis satisfies $\sin\alpha=\dfrac{|2|}{7}=\dfrac27$.

questions.q: The distance of the point $(-2,4,-5)$ from the line $\dfrac{x+3}{3}=\dfrac{y-4}{5}=\dfrac{z+8}{6}$ is
questions.explanation: Taking the vector from the line's point $(-3,4,-8)$ to the given point, $(1,0,3)$, and removing its component along the direction $(3,5,6)$, the perpendicular component has magnitude $\sqrt{37/10}$.

questions.q: The vector equation of the plane which is at a distance of $\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{14}}$ from the origin and the normal from the origin is $2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ is
questions.explanation: The unit normal is $\dfrac{2\hat i-3\hat j+\hat k}{\sqrt{14}}$, so the plane equation $\vec r\cdot\hat n=d$ becomes $\vec r\cdot(2\hat i-3\hat j+\hat k)=3$.

questions.q: Find the co-ordinates of the foot of the perpendicular drawn from the origin to the plane $5y + 8 = 0$:
questions.explanation: The plane $y=-8/5$ is parallel to the xz-plane, so the foot of the perpendicular from the origin is $(0,-8/5,0)$.

questions.q: If $\cos\alpha, \cos\beta, \cos\gamma$ are the direction cosines of a vector $\vec a$, then $\cos2\alpha + \cos2\beta + \cos2\gamma$ is equal to
questions.explanation: $\cos^2\alpha+\cos^2\beta+\cos^2\gamma=1$, so $\sum(2\cos^2-1)=2(1)-3=-1$.

questions.q: Equation of line passing through the point $(2, 3, 1)$ and parallel to the line of intersection of the plane $x - 2y - z + 5 = 0$ and $x + y + 3z = 6$ is
questions.explanation: Direction of the line of intersection $=\vec n_1\times\vec n_2=(1,-2,-1)\times(1,1,3)=(-5,-4,3)$, giving option (2).

questions.q: Foot of perpendicular drawn from the origin to the plane $2x - 3y + 4z = 29$ is ____
The distance of the point P(a, b, c) from the x-axis is
questions.explanation: Distance of a point from the x-axis is $\sqrt{y^2+z^2} = \sqrt{b^2+c^2}$.

questions.q: Equation of the plane perpendicular to the line $\dfrac{x}{1}=\dfrac{y}{2}=\dfrac{z}{3}$ and passing through the point (2, 3, 4) is
questions.explanation: The line's direction ratios (1,2,3) are the plane's normal, so the plane is $1(x-2)+2(y-3)+3(z-4)=0 \Rightarrow x+2y+3z=20$.

questions.q: The line $\dfrac{x-2}{3}=\dfrac{y-3}{4}=\dfrac{z-4}{5}$ is parallel to the plane
questions.explanation: A line is parallel to a plane when its direction ratios (3,4,5) are perpendicular to the plane's normal. For option (2), normal (2,1,-2): $2(3)+1(4)-2(5)=0$.

questions.q: The angle between two diagonals of a cube is
questions.explanation: Taking diagonal direction vectors like (1,1,1) and (-1,1,1), $\cos\theta = \dfrac{|{-1+1+1}|}{3} = \dfrac{1}{3}$, so $\theta=\cos^{-1}(1/3)$.

questions.q: Lines $\dfrac{x-2}{1}=\dfrac{y-3}{1}=\dfrac{z-4}{-K}$ and $\dfrac{x-1}{K}=\dfrac{y-4}{2}=\dfrac{z-5}{1}$ are coplanar if
questions.explanation: Setting the scalar triple product of $(P_2-P_1)$, $(1,1,-K)$ and $(K,2,1)$ to zero gives $-K^2-3K=0$, so $K=0$ or $K=-3$; $K=0$ is listed.
